tts_summary:
Here is your midday market update for Tuesday September 22nd.

Markets are stuck in a holding pattern. The S&P 500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, and the Dow is lagging, down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is hovering around a hundred dollars a barrel, slipping modestly on hopes that United Nations diplomacy could ease tension around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. Gold, silver, and bitcoin are all fractionally lower.

The big macro story is the Middle East. Iran has reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps toward easing military pressure. Meanwhile Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline appears to be partially coming back online after Houthi and Iran-aligned militia attacks disrupted the bypass route. This is keeping energy markets in a watchful but not panicked posture. Separately, Trump's approval rating has fallen to a career low of 32% in a new Reuters poll, with Republican approval tumbling to 73% from 82% the prior week.

On the company side, AutoZone beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the quality of the beat is poor. Strip out the tariff refund tailwind and the non-cash LIFO benefit and the picture looks worse. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% against expectations of plus 3.1%. The stock is still rallying though because management said comp linearity through the quarter was positive.

MillerKnoll was the cleaner beat of the morning — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and they would have beaten even without the tariff refund tailwind. That is a genuine upside quarter. THOR Industries on the other hand missed, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year and management citing a tough macro backdrop for RVs.

Viking Therapeutics is a standout on the clinical side — their GLP-1 drug VK2735 showed 22% weight loss in trial results, a strong number that keeps them firmly in the obesity drug race.

Meta is the stock to watch into the close and tomorrow. Muse, the company's personal AI agent, is seeing surging downloads. Shopify just agreed to let Muse complete purchases on its platform, a direct shot at Amazon which blocked Muse. Zuckerberg's keynote at the Meta Connect conference tomorrow night at 7pm Eastern is the first in a string of critical AI catalysts — OpenAI DevDay on September 29th and Micron earnings on September 30th follow right behind.

On the negative side, Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp are getting hit hard after CMS released Medicare lab service payment rates that came in with larger cuts than anticipated. Financials broadly — banks, brokers, insurers, asset managers — are all underperforming with no single catalyst, just general risk-off rotation within the market. And Texas Governor Abbott halting new data center permits is adding a low-level overhang on AI infrastructure names.

The bottom line for the rest of today's session is that direction is unclear until the geopolitical picture around Iran develops further. The AI catalyst window starting tomorrow night is the real driver to watch. Stay disciplined, manage size, and let the catalysts come to you.
